newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends sharply down, Dec/Jan in contango.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends sharply down, Dec/Jan in contango.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed down heavily on Monday, with the front month's weakness pushing Dec/Jan into contango.
Dec gas oil closed $8.50 a tonne lower at $215.50, while Jan shed $7.50 to end the session at $216.50.

Brokers said the end of strikes at Elf refineries in France, forecasts of moderate weather in the U.S., and talk of heavy buying on January by a Wall Street trader combined to push the market into contango for the first time since August.
Some suggested that trading house Cargill, the main lifter of the record Nov delivery was selling heavy spot volumes.
The Dec contract, which expires on Thursday, failed to break below support at $215.50.
Jan Brent was trading 64 cents down on the day at $23.90 a barrel at 1739 GMT, off a session low of $23.77.
U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Monday sent notification to the Security Council enabling the oil-for-food deal to enter into force at 0501 GMT on Tuesday, a U.N. spokesman said.
"It's moving down in thin volumes. It climbed 50 cents in the last ten minutes on Friday so this is the correction you'd expect regardless of the headlines," a broker said.
The next technical support level for Brent below $23.90 was pegged at $23.48.
"The next hurdle is the Iraqi oil sale. No ships have as yet been chartered, so crudes may not hit the market as fast as implied," said Charles Gray of Prudential Bache futures
